Format checklist, one-paragraph essence, self-check tasks.
examShortTricks: Trick 1: The extended metaphor: life = drama, people = actors, God = playwright — state the controlling metaphor before anything else.
Trick 2: The seven ages in order: infant, schoolboy, lover, soldier, justice, pantaloon (old man), second childhood — memorise the list; sequencing questions are guaranteed.
Trick 3: The last age is the harshest: sans teeth, sans eyes, sans taste, sans everything — the repetition 'sans' drives the message of decline; quote it.
practiceQuestions: Q. List the seven ages of man. (3 marks) — infant, schoolboy, lover, soldier, justice, pantaloon, second childhood.
Q. What is the message of the poem? (2 marks) — life is a predictable performance from entry to exit; humans merely play their parts.
keyPoints: Extended metaphor: life as theatre; the seven ages are seven acts.
Know the stages in order — infant, schoolboy, lover, soldier, justice, pantaloon, second childhood.
